userStories.title: Negotiate legacy ACP modes/models and enforce Gemini read-only profiles with plan mode
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add legacy session mode/model negotiation and enable Gemini none/read/review through its plan mode without changing config-option-first behavior.

**Motivation** — `session/new` returns `{ sessionId, modes, models }` and no `configOptions`.

**Approach** — Implement the following Target design; Baseline descriptions are location hints only, never the interface to implement.

- `AcpLink` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/connection.ts`)
  - Target: adds `setMode(params: SetSessionModeRequest): Promise<SetSessionModeResponse>` (sent as `methods.agent.session.setMode`) and `setModel(params: { readonly sessionId: string; readonly modelId: string }): Promise<unknown>` (sent as the method string `SET_MODEL_METHOD = "session/set_model"` through the SDK's `request(method: string, params)` overload).
- New module `packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/session-offers.ts`:
  - `export interface SessionOffers { readonly configOptions: readonly SessionConfigOption[]; readonly modeIds: readonly string[]; readonly modelIds: readonly string[] }`
  - `export function sessionOffers(response: unknown): SessionOffers` — reads `configOptions` (as today: the array when present, else `[]`), `modes.availableModes[].id` and `models.availableModels[].modelId` from an untyped `session/new`, `session/resume` or `session/load` response. Entries that are not non-empty strings are skipped; a missing or malformed block yields `[]`.
- `newSession` (`open.ts`) and `checkRestored` (`resume.ts`)
  - Target: each returns `offers: SessionOffers` built with `sessionOffers(response)` (a null restore answer yields empty offers) in place of `configOptions`.
- `applyConfig`, `applyMode`, `applyModel`, `applyEffort` (`open.ts`)
  - Target: thread `SessionOffers`. `applyMode`: the config-option path is tried first, unchanged; otherwise, when `offers.modeIds` includes `mode.value`, it sends `session/set_mode { sessionId, modeId: mode.value }` (the `configId` is not used on this path); otherwise the same refusal as today. `applyModel`: the config-option path first, unchanged; otherwise, when `offers.modelIds` includes the model, it sends `session/set_model { sessionId, modelId }`; otherwise the refusal, whose offered list is the config-option model values followed by `offers.modelIds`, each id cleaned as today and the combined list capped at the existing `MAX_OFFERED_MODELS` (50) entries. `applyEffort` keeps working on `offers.configOptions` only.
- Registry entry `gemini` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/registry.ts`)
  - Target: same launch and auth env; `readOnly: { mode: { configId: "mode", value: "plan" }, disallowedTools: [], sessionOptions: {}, launchEnv: {} }`; `defaultMode` and `preApproval` undefined.

Symbols this feature only reads:

- `modeFor(profile, entry)` in `packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/capabilities.ts`: `none`/`read`/`review` → `entry.readOnly.mode`, other profiles → `entry.defaultMode`.
- `offersValue(options, configId, value)`, `modelOptionId(options, model)` and `selectValues(option)` in `capabilities.ts`.
- `unmetRequirement(record, req)` refuses a read-only profile when `record.readOnlyMode` is false; `buildCapabilityRecord(init, entry)` sets `readOnlyMode` to `entry?.readOnly !== undefined`.
- `routerFor` / `sandboxFor` give the permission layer a sandbox only when `entry?.preApproval` is defined; gemini has none.

Extend the fake agent so a script can return `modes` and `models` blocks from `session/new` and restore answers and records `session/set_mode` and `session/set_model`, with exported `GEMINI_SESSION_MODES` and `GEMINI_SESSION_MODELS` fixtures; put this story's integration tests in a new `test/unit/client/backend-gemini.test.ts`. Claude, codex and opencode behaviour does not change.

Fixture design: `FakeScript` gains optional `modes` and `models` blocks returned by session/new, session/resume and session/load, typed as plain records so the untyped `models` block passes through, and optional `setModeFailure` and `setModelFailure` (each an `RpcFailure`, like `newSessionFailure`); exports `GEMINI_SESSION_MODES` (available `default`, `autoEdit`, `yolo`, `plan`; current `default`) and `GEMINI_SESSION_MODELS` (available `auto`, `gemini-3-flash-preview`; current `auto`); no existing export changes. The fake returns the script's `modes`/`models` blocks from session/new and `restoredResponse`, and handles session/set_mode and session/set_model by recording their params and answering `{}`, or throwing the script's `setModeFailure` / `setModelFailure` as a JSON-RPC error when set; the `models` block is returned through a widened object, since the SDK's session/new response type has no `models` field. Use the custom-method `onRequest(method, parser, handler)` overload for the untyped method.

Regression updates: move Gemini out of registry.test.ts's no-read-only-enforcement table into its own test; pi stays. Change capabilities.test.ts's unsupported `readOnlyFor("none", registryEntry("gemini"))` example to pi. Change backend-permissions.test.ts's agent-without-read-only-enforcement example from gemini to pi, keeping refusal after initialize with capability profile for read/none. Update checkRestored exact-object, offered-options and null-answer expectations in resume.test.ts to `offers: { configOptions: <same>, modeIds: [], modelIds: [] }`, keeping the same invariants.

Failure handling: A config option offers the mode or model → The config-option path is used, exactly as today; the session `modes`/`models` blocks are not consulted. Neither a config option nor the session `modes` block offers the read-only mode → Existing refusal: `AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`, capability `profile`, process killed. Neither a config option nor the session `models` block offers the requested model → Existing refusal: capability `model`; the offered list now includes the `models` block's ids. The agent answers `session/set_mode` or `session/set_model` with a JSON-RPC error → The open fails as any other failed open step does today (the step's error, process killed). gemini asks permission for a write or shell command (possible only outside `plan` mode, e.g. `full`) → Decided by profile as today (`full` allows); gemini continues after a reject.

Seam: `sessionOffers` (new export of `session-offers.ts`) is consumed by `newSession` and `checkRestored` in the same story; its seam ACs enter at `createAgentSession` with `acpBackend({ agent: "gemini" })` against a fake that returns `modes`/`models` blocks and assert on the recorded `session/set_mode` / `session/set_model` calls. Use inMemoryAgent and _acpBackendDeps.launch, never a real agent. Preserve configOptions refreshes from config-option setters while retaining legacy offer lists for later stages. All setter requests use the existing bounded open-step path and failed-open cleanup. The step's error means the existing classified AgentSessionError, not a raw RequestError: a generic JSON-RPC failure is AGENT_SESSION_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE with context.step and context.rpcCode (errors.ts openRequestError). Permission rejection/continuation is exercised with an ask-profile fake that records the caller's reject_once choice and then finishes end_turn; assert the facade's turn_end status completed and output, not a raw ACP end_turn status on a facade event.

**Scope** — In: ACP link, offer parsing, open/restore configuration, Gemini registry policy, fake protocol support and corresponding behavioral/regression tests. Out: US-002's nax configuration and isolated-home launch environment. gemini's `plan` mode writing plan `.md` files into its own plans directory under the gemini home (`.gemini/tmp/…/plans`); those writes never reach the repository and nax does not block them. gemini's model routing when no model is set: with `auto` it may route `plan`-mode turns to a Pro model, which costs more free-tier quota; nax sets no model unless configured. A gemini release that renames `session/set_model`, changes the `models` block shape, or moves auth files; nax does not detect it. Updating the package context file `.nax/mono/packages/nax-agent-acp/context.md` to say gemini is read-only capable: a manual step after merge, since `.nax/` is read-only to the run. Applying nax's embedder sandbox to gemini, or letting a gemini reviewer run shell commands: under `review` gemini runs in `plan` mode, which offers no shell tool (accepted 2026-10-17). Read-only enforcement for pi (the rest of nathapp-io/nax#2372); this spec does not close that issue. Reasoning effort on gemini: it offers no effort config option, so a configured effort is skipped as for any agent that does not offer one. A live check against a real gemini process: a maintainer step after merge (Google-login and stored-key isolation can only be checked with such an account).

**Interface** —
```typescript
setMode(params: SetSessionModeRequest): Promise<SetSessionModeResponse>
setModel(params: { readonly sessionId: string; readonly modelId: string }): Promise<unknown>
export interface SessionOffers { readonly configOptions: readonly SessionConfigOption[]; readonly modeIds: readonly string[]; readonly modelIds: readonly string[] }
export function sessionOffers(response: unknown): SessionOffers
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] sessionOffers({ sessionId: "s", modes: { availableModes: [{ id: "default", name: "Default" }, { id: "plan", name: "Plan" }], currentModeId: "default" }, models: { availableModels: [{ modelId: "auto", name: "Auto" }, { modelId: "m2", name: "M2" }], currentModelId: "auto" } }) returns { configOptions: [], modeIds: ["default", "plan"], modelIds: ["auto", "m2"] }.
[unit] sessionOffers returns the response's configOptions array when present.

[unit] sessionOffers(null), sessionOffers({}) and sessionOffers({ modes: "x", models: { availableModels: [{ modelId: 3 }, { modelId: "" }, {}] } }) each return { configOptions: [], modeIds: [], modelIds: [] }.
[unit] registryEntry("gemini")?.readOnly equals { mode: { configId: "mode", value: "plan" }, disallowedTools: [], sessionOptions: {}, launchEnv: {} }.
[unit] registryEntry("gemini")?.defaultMode is undefined.
[unit] registryEntry("gemini")?.preApproval is undefined.
[unit] modeFor(profile, registryEntry("gemini")) returns { configId: "mode", value: "plan" } for each profile in ["read", "none", "review"].
[unit] modeFor("full", registryEntry("gemini")) is undefined.

[unit] unmetRequirement(buildCapabilityRecord(init, registryEntry("gemini")), { profile: "read", toolCount: 0, resume: false }) is undefined when init is an initialize response with no MCP capabilities.

[unit] unmetRequirement(buildCapabilityRecord(init, registryEntry("gemini")), { profile: "review", toolCount: 0, resume: false }) is undefined when init is an initialize response with no MCP capabilities.
[integration] createAgentSession with acpBackend({ agent: "gemini", ... }), profile read and a fake script with modes: GEMINI_SESSION_MODES and no configOptions opens successfully.
[integration] When that read-profile Gemini session opens, the fake records exactly one session/set_mode call with { sessionId: "fake-session-1", modeId: "plan" }.
[integration] When that read-profile Gemini session opens, the fake records no session/set_config_option call.
[integration] When the same Gemini session opens with profile review or none, each open records one session/set_mode call with modeId "plan".
[integration] When Gemini opens with profile full against the same modes-only fake, the fake records no session/set_mode call.

[integration] When Gemini opens with profile read against a fake whose modes block has no plan mode and no config option offers plan, the open is refused with AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED and capability profile.
[integration] When Gemini's read-profile open is refused because plan is absent, the agent process is killed once.
[integration] createAgentSession with Gemini, model "gemini-3-flash-preview", profile full and a fake script with models: GEMINI_SESSION_MODELS and no configOptions opens successfully.
[integration] When that modeled full-profile Gemini session opens, the fake records exactly one session/set_model call with modelId "gemini-3-flash-preview".
[integration] When Gemini opens with model "gemini-9" and profile full against the same models-only fake, the open is refused with capability model.
[integration] When that unknown-model open is refused, the refusal's offered list contains "auto" and "gemini-3-flash-preview".

[integration] When Claude opens with profile read and model "sonnet" against a fake offering CLAUDE_CONFIG_OPTIONS and also a modes block containing default, the fake records the mode and the model through session/set_config_option only, preserving config-option precedence.
[integration] When that Claude open offers config options and a modes block, the fake records neither session/set_mode nor session/set_model.

[integration] When codex opens with profile read against a fake offering CODEX_CONFIG_OPTIONS, it still records one session/set_config_option call with value "read-only" (regression anchor: already true on main).
[integration] When that codex session opens, it records no session/set_mode call (regression anchor: already true on main).

[integration] When a Gemini session is restored with profile read and modes: GEMINI_SESSION_MODES against a fake advertising only loadSession, the fake records one session/set_mode call with modeId "plan" after session/load.

[integration] When a Gemini session is restored with profile read and modes: GEMINI_SESSION_MODES against a fake advertising session resume, the fake records one session/set_mode call with modeId "plan" after session/resume.

[integration] When Gemini opens with profile read, modes: GEMINI_SESSION_MODES and setModeFailure: { code: -32603, message: "mode failed" }, createAgentSession rejects with AGENT_SESSION_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE and context { step: "session/set_mode", rpcCode: -32603 }, preserving the existing open-step error classification.
[integration] When that session/set_mode step fails, the agent process is killed once.

[integration] When Gemini opens with model "gemini-3-flash-preview", profile full, models: GEMINI_SESSION_MODELS and setModelFailure: { code: -32603, message: "model failed" }, createAgentSession rejects with AGENT_SESSION_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE and context { step: "session/set_model", rpcCode: -32603 }, preserving the existing open-step error classification.
[integration] When that session/set_model step fails, the agent process is killed once.
[integration] When Gemini opens with model "gemini-9", profile full and a fake models block listing 60 ids with no configOptions, the open is refused with capability model.
[integration] When that 60-id model offer is refused, the refusal's offered list has exactly 50 entries, starting with the fake's first model id.
[integration] In a Gemini session opened with profile full, a session/request_permission for an execute tool call is answered with the allow_once option.
[integration] When that full-profile execute permission is decided, the decision is recorded with reason FULL_REASON.
[integration] When Gemini opens with profile read and one embedder tool, the open is refused with AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED and capability tools.

[integration] When a config option offers a requested mode even though a session modes block also offers it, the mode is set through session/set_config_option exactly as today, without using session/set_mode.

[integration] When a config option offers a requested model even though a session models block also offers it, the model is set through session/set_config_option exactly as today, without using session/set_model.
[integration] When neither config options nor the session models block offers the requested model, the failed open kills the agent process.

[integration] In a Gemini session opened with profile full, when the fake requests permission for an edit tool call offering allow_once and reject_once, the fake records permission-outcome { outcome: "selected", optionId: "opt-allow_once" }, preserving the existing full profile decision.

[integration] Given a Gemini session opened with profile ask and a fake execute permission offering allow_once and reject_once, when the caller denies the request, the fake records permission-outcome { outcome: "selected", optionId: "opt-reject_once" }, preserving the existing profile-based decision behavior outside plan mode.

[integration] Given that caller-denied Gemini ask-profile permission followed by fake text "continued" and stopReason end_turn, endOf(await driveTurn(session, "go")) returns a turn_end matching { status: "completed", output: "continued" }, proving a rejected tool call does not itself abort the turn; a real Gemini live check remains a maintainer step.

routing.reasoning: Multi-module protocol fallback across connection, session creation/restoration and registry policy, with fake-agent integration and compatibility anchors; session access control requires the security override and strict test isolation.

suggestedCriteria: When a mode config-option setter returns a new configOptions array offering the requested model, the following model selection uses that returned array rather than the initial one.
When a mode config-option setter returns updated configOptions without the requested model but the original models block offers it, model selection still sends session/set_model.

When a model refusal combines config-option values with legacy models containing secrets or control characters, its offered list preserves config-option-first order and exposes only cleaned, secret-scrubbed ids.
When a Gemini session is reconnected after process death and the restore response offers plan through modes, the replacement agent receives session/set_mode with modeId plan before the next prompt.
When sessionOffers receives mixed valid and invalid mode and model entries, its modeIds and modelIds retain only non-empty string ids in source order.

modifiedFiles.reason: `AcpLink` gains `setMode` and `setModel`; `openConnection` implements them; exports `SET_MODEL_METHOD`.
`newSession` returns `offers`; `applyConfig`, `applyMode`, `applyModel` and `applyEffort` take `SessionOffers`; `applyMode` and `applyModel` gain the session/set_mode / session/set_model fallback.
`RestoredSession` carries `offers: SessionOffers` (built with `sessionOffers`) in place of `configOptions`.
the gemini entry gets `readOnly` with mode `plan`.

`FakeScript` gains optional `modes` and `models` blocks returned by session/new, session/resume and session/load, typed as plain records so the untyped `models` block passes through, and optional `setModeFailure` and `setModelFailure` (each an `RpcFailure`, like `newSessionFailure`); exports `GEMINI_SESSION_MODES` (available `default`, `autoEdit`, `yolo`, `plan`; current `default`) and `GEMINI_SESSION_MODELS` (available `auto`, `gemini-3-flash-preview`; current `auto`); no existing export changes.

returns the script's `modes`/`models` blocks from session/new and `restoredResponse`, and handles session/set_mode and session/set_model by recording their params and answering `{}`, or throwing the script's `setModeFailure` / `setModelFailure` as a JSON-RPC error when set; the `models` block is returned through a widened object, since the SDK's session/new response type has no `models` field.

the table test "%s: launch candidates and auth env; no read-only enforcement, no pre-approval" lists gemini with `readOnly: undefined`, so gemini moves out of that table into its own test asserting the new `readOnly` (pi stays).
the test asserting `readOnlyFor("none", registryEntry("gemini"))` is undefined switches to `registryEntry("pi")`, keeping the invariant that an agent without enforcement yields undefined.

the test "%s on an agent without a read-only mode: refused after initialize" opens `agent: "gemini"`; it switches to `agent: "pi"`, keeping the invariant that `read`/`none` on an agent without read-only enforcement is refused after `initialize` with capability `profile`.

the `checkRestored` tests assert the result's `configOptions` field (the exact-object test for a resumed id, the load test returning the offered options, and the null-answer test); they assert `offers` instead: `{ configOptions: <same>, modeIds: [], modelIds: [] }`, keeping the same invariants.

userStories.title: Optionally isolate Gemini home while sharing only credentials and auth type
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Parsing a config with agent.acp unset yields agent.acp.gemini equal to { isolateHome: false }.
[unit] Parsing a config with agent.acp unset yields codex: { isolateHome: false, fullMode: "workspace-write" } and opencode: { isolateConfig: false }, keeping their existing defaults unchanged.
[unit] Parsing a config with agent.acp.gemini.isolateHome: "yes" fails validation with an issue whose path ends in isolateHome.
[unit] geminiAcpSettings(undefined) and geminiAcpSettings({}) each return { isolateHome: false }.
[unit] geminiAcpSettings({ agent: { acp: { gemini: { isolateHome: true } } } }) returns { isolateHome: true }.
[unit] isolatedGeminiHomeDir() returns join(globalConfigDir(), "acp", "gemini-home").

[unit] Given env("GEMINI_CLI_HOME") is undefined, homedir() is "/u", both source credentials files are regular files, both isolated entries are absent and source settings contain {"security":{"auth":{"selectedType":"oauth-personal"}},"mcpServers":{"x":{}}}, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() calls mkdir with <isolated>/.gemini.
[unit] Given those same source files and settings, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() calls symlink("/u/.gemini/oauth_creds.json", <isolated>/.gemini/oauth_creds.json).
[unit] Given those same source files and settings, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() calls symlink("/u/.gemini/gemini-credentials.json", <isolated>/.gemini/gemini-credentials.json).

[unit] Given those same source files and settings, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() writes <isolated>/.gemini/settings.json with exactly {"security":{"auth":{"selectedType":"oauth-personal"}}}, excluding mcpServers.
[unit] Given those same source files and settings, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() returns isolatedGeminiHomeDir().

[unit] When env("GEMINI_CLI_HOME") returns "/custom" and that home's .gemini/oauth_creds.json is present with no isolated entry, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() uses symlink target "/custom/.gemini/oauth_creds.json".

[unit] When env("GEMINI_CLI_HOME") returns "", homedir() returns "/u", /u/.gemini/oauth_creds.json is a regular file and its isolated entry is absent, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() calls symlink with target "/u/.gemini/oauth_creds.json", using <homedir()>/.gemini as the source.
[unit] When entryExists is true for an isolated credentials entry, including a dangling link, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() does not call symlink for that entry.
[unit] When fileExists is false for a source credentials file, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() does not call symlink for that file.

[unit] When source settings readText returns undefined, JSON without security.auth.selectedType, JSON with numeric or empty-string selectedType, or a JSON array or null, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() writes no settings file.

[unit] When source settings readText returns undefined, JSON without security.auth.selectedType, JSON with numeric or empty-string selectedType, or a JSON array or null, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() logs no warn.
[unit] When source settings readText returns text that is not JSON, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() writes no settings file.
[unit] When source settings readText returns text that is not JSON, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() calls warn exactly once.

[unit] When the isolated settings.json already exists under entryExists and source settings carry selectedType "gemini-api-key", prepareIsolatedGeminiHome() still writes the isolated file with exactly {"security":{"auth":{"selectedType":"gemini-api-key"}}}, rewritten on every call.

[unit] withGeminiAcpEnv({ provider: "gemini", model: "m", env: { A: "1" } }, "gemini", { isolateHome: true }) returns a new def whose env equals { A: "1", GEMINI_CLI_HOME: isolatedGeminiHomeDir() } when preparation succeeds.
[unit] When withGeminiAcpEnv injects the isolated home into that def, the input's env remains equal to { A: "1" }.

[unit] withGeminiAcpEnv(def, "gemini", { isolateHome: false }), withGeminiAcpEnv(def, "claude", { isolateHome: true }) and withGeminiAcpEnv(def, undefined, { isolateHome: true }) each return def itself.
[unit] Those disabled or non-Gemini withGeminiAcpEnv calls invoke no _geminiAcpEnvDeps function.

[unit] withGeminiAcpEnv({ provider: "p", model: "m" }, "gemini", { isolateHome: true }) returns a def whose env equals { GEMINI_CLI_HOME: isolatedGeminiHomeDir() } when preparation succeeds, even though the input has no env.
[unit] withGeminiAcpEnv({ provider: "p", model: "m", env: { GEMINI_CLI_HOME: "/mine" } }, "gemini", { isolateHome: true }) returns a def whose env.GEMINI_CLI_HOME remains "/mine".
[unit] When the model env already sets GEMINI_CLI_HOME to "/mine", withGeminiAcpEnv calls no _geminiAcpEnvDeps filesystem function.
[unit] When the model env sets GEMINI_CLI_HOME to an empty string, withGeminiAcpEnv preserves that empty-string value.
[unit] When the model env sets GEMINI_CLI_HOME to an empty string, withGeminiAcpEnv calls no _geminiAcpEnvDeps filesystem function.

[unit] When _geminiAcpEnvDeps.mkdir throws, withGeminiAcpEnv(def, "gemini", { isolateHome: true }) returns def itself without adding GEMINI_CLI_HOME, so the session runs on the user's Gemini home (fail open).
[unit] When _geminiAcpEnvDeps.mkdir throws during that call, _geminiAcpEnvDeps.warn is called exactly once.
[unit] acpEnvSettings({ agent: { acp: { gemini: { isolateHome: true } } } }).gemini equals { isolateHome: true }.
[unit] acpEnvSettings(undefined).gemini equals { isolateHome: false }.

[unit] withAcpEnv(def, "gemini", { codex: { isolateHome: true, fullMode: "agent-full-access" }, opencode: { isolateConfig: true }, gemini: { isolateHome: true } }) returns a def whose env.GEMINI_CLI_HOME equals isolatedGeminiHomeDir() when preparation succeeds.
[unit] When that Gemini withAcpEnv call starts without unrelated launch env keys, its returned env contains none of INITIAL_AGENT_MODE, CODEX_HOME or OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR.

[unit] withAcpEnv(def, "codex", { codex: { isolateHome: false, fullMode: "workspace-write" }, opencode: { isolateConfig: false }, gemini: { isolateHome: true } }) returns a def whose env.INITIAL_AGENT_MODE equals "workspace-write".
[unit] When that codex withAcpEnv call starts without GEMINI_CLI_HOME, its returned env has no GEMINI_CLI_HOME.

[integration] When SessionManager.openSession uses agentName "gemini" and config agent.acp.gemini.isolateHome true with _geminiAcpEnvDeps stubbed, it calls the adapter's openSession with options.modelDef.env.GEMINI_CLI_HOME equal to isolatedGeminiHomeDir().

[unit] Given source settings.json is unparseable and all filesystem operations otherwise succeed, withGeminiAcpEnv({ env: { GEMINI_API_KEY: "test-key" } }, "gemini", { isolateHome: true }) returns a def whose env equals { GEMINI_API_KEY: "test-key", GEMINI_CLI_HOME: isolatedGeminiHomeDir() }, leaving Gemini's own API-key auth default available without asserting a live authentication result.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module schema/default/runtime wiring plus credential-sharing filesystem preparation, fail-open policy and launch-env integration; credentials and session isolation require the security override and strict test isolation.

suggestedCriteria: When the first preparation writes oauth-personal selectedType and a later source settings file has no selectedType, prepareIsolatedGeminiHome leaves the previously written isolated settings file unchanged.

When a symlink, source-settings read or isolated-settings write raises a filesystem error, withGeminiAcpEnv returns the exact input and emits one preparation warning without injecting GEMINI_CLI_HOME.
When completeAsWithFallback resolves a Gemini model with isolateHome true and stubbed preparation succeeds, the adapter receives modelDef.env.GEMINI_CLI_HOME equal to isolatedGeminiHomeDir().
When a model-def env contains GEMINI_CLI_HOME, withGeminiAcpEnv returns the exact input object rather than cloning it.

analysis:
Existing enhancement, not greenfield. Navigation: codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this session; findings were verified with direct reads and text searches rooted at the supplied execution repository. The binding decomposition is exactly US-001 in packages/nax-agent-acp and US-002 in packages/nax, both with no dependencies. They can proceed independently: the first changes ACP negotiation and Gemini profile support; the second adds an opt-in nax launch environment. Both involve security-sensitive sessions or credentials and therefore require three-session-tdd with strict test/implementation isolation. Their multi-module integration scope is complex, not an architectural rewrite. native-deepseek is the lowest-cost listed profile whose strengths cover these explicit multi-file integrations; escalate only if implementation encounters unresolved convention or protocol issues.

US-001 architecture and impact: packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/connection.ts:40 defines AcpLink; :55 constructs openConnection and :64 forwards outbound calls through SDK agent.request. Add typed setMode through methods.agent.session.setMode and untyped setModel through exported SET_MODEL_METHOD = "session/set_model". Do not import the SDK experimental entry or add dependencies. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/open.ts:79 defines Established with configOptions; :177 establishes sessions; :200 applies session configuration after either creation or restore; :216 creates a new session and reads only created.configOptions. Replace that internal carrier with offers: SessionOffers from the new parser, for creation and restoration alike. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/resume.ts:43 defines RestoredSession, :117 checkRestored checks echoed identity and returns configuration, and :144 restoreSession prefers session/resume over session/load. Preserve identity validation, stored cwd, transcript behavior, replay behavior and resume selection, including null restore answers; only the offer carrier changes. Reconnect also uses this restore/open flow and must not lose offers.

packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/open.ts:258 applies mode, model, then effort; :264 applyMode currently refuses missing config-option values; :283 offeredModels caps agent-supplied display data at 50 ids, cleaning labels with a 100-character limit; :293 applyModel refuses models absent from config options; :317 applyEffort warns and skips unsupported effort. Keep config-option precedence and continue using any configOptions returned by a setter for subsequent model/effort selection. Thread SessionOffers while retaining modeIds/modelIds when configOptions are refreshed. Legacy mode/model RPC responses are empty and must not erase offers. Combine config-option model values before legacy model ids for refusals, preserve sanitization and the existing 50-entry cap, and never set a model unless configured. The parser is an unknown-input boundary: malformed or absent blocks yield empty arrays, invalid/empty ids are skipped, and a present configOptions array remains the existing data source. Do not invent an effort fallback.

packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/capabilities.ts:49 builds capabilities from initialize plus registry data; :82 unmetRequirement checks profile first, then HTTP MCP plus pre-approval for tools, then restoration support. :97 selectValues, :102 offersValue and :107 modelOptionId are existing selectors to reuse unchanged. :137 readOnlyFor and :145 modeFor already select the registry read-only entry for none/read/review. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/registry.ts:149 currently registers Gemini with only gemini --acp and GEMINI_API_KEY. Adding its readOnly mode plan makes none/read/review admissible without changing the capability algorithms. Keep defaultMode/preApproval undefined and launch/auth unchanged. Gemini still cannot pre-approve embedder tools. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/open.ts:226 sandboxFor returns nothing without preApproval, and :243 sessionSetup depends on that channel; do not route Gemini into the embedder sandbox or relax tools admission. Every failure inside establish is already cleaned up by the kill/close catch at open.ts:125; legacy setter errors must use the same bounded step/error path at :151 rather than bypassing timeout, abort, redaction or cleanup.

Extend this data-only script with optional modes/models plain records and setter RpcFailure fields; add GEMINI_SESSION_MODES/GEMINI_SESSION_MODELS without altering existing exports. packages/nax-agent-acp/test/fixtures/fake-agent/agent.ts:221 restoredResponse and :254 buildFakeAgent serve both in-process and subprocess tests; :273 session/new, :279 resume, :285 load and :292 setConfigOption currently only carry config options. Use the custom-method parser overload for set_model. packages/nax-agent-acp/test/unit/client/backend-opencode.test.ts:74 demonstrates inMemoryAgent, _acpBackendDeps.launch and createAgentSession, with cleanup at :32; mirror that pattern for backend-gemini.test.ts. Unit tests for the parser belong in session-offers.test.ts. Update existing regression anchors rather than deleting them: registry.test.ts:38 currently includes Gemini in the no-enforcement table; capabilities.test.ts:167 expects no Gemini enforcement; backend-permissions.test.ts:138-144 uses Gemini as the unsupported-profile agent. Move the latter invariants to pi and give Gemini its own registry expectations. resume.test.ts:132, :138 and :148 assert configOptions and must assert offers with empty legacy arrays instead. Claude/codex/opencode configuration, permissions and effort behavior remain unchanged. No real agent process is permitted in unit tests; use launch injection and existing transcript/event/error helpers. Cover both restoration protocols, failed-open kill counts, combined model diagnostics, full-profile permission decisions and unsupported embedder tools at the facade seam.

US-002 architecture and impact: packages/nax/src/config/schemas-infra.ts:344 and :355 hold the codex/opencode default constants; :361 AgentAcpConfigSchema defines the launch settings; :477 has one literal acp default. This file is currently 591 lines and must grow by at most four lines, staying below 600. Put the new Gemini schema/default in schemas-acp-agents.ts and import it instead of expanding inline configuration. Text search confirms the second literal default at packages/nax/src/config/schemas.ts:371-376, the config barrel default exports at packages/nax/src/config/index.ts:116, and AgentAcpConfig at packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types-agent.ts:90 with opencode at :119. Update all of these together so unset, partial and runtime configs agree on isolateHome false; runtime Gemini fields are optional for compatibility. packages/nax/src/config/paths/index.ts:63 is the existing globalConfigDir helper; use it rather than spelling ~/.nax inline.

packages/nax/src/agents/shared/acp-env.ts:25 defines AcpEnvSettings, :31 reads config and :40 composes injections, currently codex then opencode. Add Gemini last. packages/nax/src/agents/shared/codex-acp-env.ts:71 reads settings with schema-default fallbacks, :84 computes the isolated home, :115 prepares shared credentials using lstat/stat semantics, :145 injects without mutating the model def, and :169 exposes every environment/fs/logger operation through a deps seam. Follow this precedent while respecting the target Gemini interface: GEMINI_CLI_HOME names a home containing .gemini, unlike CODEX_HOME naming its config directory directly. Source credentials come from a non-empty process GEMINI_CLI_HOME or homedir(), each followed by .gemini; a model-def GEMINI_CLI_HOME override, including an empty string, suppresses preparation entirely. Symlink only oauth_creds.json and gemini-credentials.json when source is a regular file and the isolated entry is absent under lstat, preserving dangling links. Serialize only security.auth.selectedType from an object-shaped source settings file; valid auth type rewrites settings every call, malformed JSON warns once without writing, and missing/invalid auth type writes nothing and does not delete stale settings. All direct filesystem failures propagate from prepareIsolatedGeminiHome, but withGeminiAcpEnv catches preparation failure, warns once, and returns the exact input with no injected home. Disabled or non-Gemini calls return the input and touch no deps. No other files/settings/policies/extensions are copied.

Consumers already share the right injection point: text search confirms packages/nax/src/session/model-selection.ts:54 calls withAcpEnv; packages/nax/src/session/manager.ts:449 passes acpEnvSettings(opts.config ?? this._config) into selectModel; packages/nax/src/agents/manager-complete-as.ts:41 uses withAcpEnv with resolved configuration for completeAsWithFallback. Extend the shared module rather than duplicating injection in these consumers. Existing codex-acp-env.ts:19-21 explains that model-def env is carried into SessionModel and backendEnv. Keep configuration imports in agents/shared, never agents/acp, whose no-config boundary is enforced. Only edit the profile-map header comment to remove Gemini from the unsupported-read list; permission resolution remains resolvePermissions(config, stage). codex/opencode modules remain unchanged.

US-002 tests: packages/nax/test/unit/agents/shared/acp-env.test.ts:29 pins exact settings objects and :51 exercises withAcpEnv; add Gemini expectations and a disabled Gemini block to existing literal AcpEnvSettings callers. packages/nax/test/unit/session/model-selection.test.ts also supplies literal settings and must be updated without changing existing expectations. packages/nax/test/unit/config/agent-schema.test.ts:4 exercises NaxConfigSchema and contains the exact acp-default regression assertion; extend it for the new default and invalid boolean. packages/nax/test/unit/session/manager-phase-b-session.test.ts:108 starts openSession tests and :117 captures adapter arguments using makeAgentAdapter, giving the required integration seam above config resolution; add the Gemini acceptance test without changing existing tests. packages/nax/test/helpers/opencode-acp-deps.ts:19 illustrates fresh spies assigned to a deps object and paired with withDepsRestore; use existing helper conventions for new Gemini tests, restoring every seam and never touching the developer's real home. New behavioral env tests belong in test/unit/agents/shared/gemini-acp-env.test.ts. docs/guides/configuration.md:150 documents opencode isolation beside which the Gemini option belongs; the nearby example at :168 and explanatory text at :197 provide context. The required docs edit is root-relative even though binding US-002 workdir remains packages/nax.

Risks/backward compatibility/migration: legacy negotiation is additive and only used when the requested value is absent from config options; advertised values still gate all changes. Refreshing configOptions must not discard the legacy lists. Do not infer a current mode/model or send unsupported RPCs based solely on agent name. The default-off isolation option preserves existing environments, and explicit model-env overrides remain authoritative. Plan mode is a Gemini-owned repository read-only policy, not an unconditional security guarantee: user-scoped approvals, policies or extensions can override its default-tier denies when isolation is off; isolation can itself fail open by explicit ruling. review intentionally has no shell tool, none still uses plan, and plan files may be written only inside Gemini's own home. Auth symlinks share credentials, not arbitrary settings; stored-key decryption by hostname/username is documented upstream but not live-verified. Do not log credential contents or copy additional auth material. Existing isolated entries and stale selectedType persist intentionally, Windows symlink support is deferred, and system/admin policies remain outside this feature. No data migration, package version bump, new dependency or transcript schema migration is needed: offers are transient handshake data. API-key and Google-login live verification plus package context updates are maintainer-only post-merge steps; do not close all of #2372 because pi remains unsupported. Read docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:11-45 and applicable canonical rules before implementation; preserve package boundaries and generated-context protections. Validation uses package-scoped bun run test/typecheck/check:all and targeted tests, never bare bun test or bun run nax. This PRD generation did not run tests or modify implementation files.

Refine-pass audit: all 18 numbered US-001 and all 18 numbered US-002 spec ACs were individually enumerated and matched to the split behavioral assertions; none was dropped. The codex 'already true on main', config-option precedence, unchanged defaults, model-selection existing expectations and settings rewritten-on-every-call qualifiers remain. All eight failure-table rows have matching negative/precedence/continuation assertions and all 13 feature exclusions remain verbatim. Both stories retain exactly their binding workdirs and empty dependency arrays, all five spec-recommended context files, and the specified new-file outputs. Re-read verification adds an important interface correction: packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/errors.ts:93 openRequestError wraps generic JSON-RPC errors as AGENT_SESSION_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE with context.step/rpcCode, so setter-failure ACs now assert the classified error rather than implying raw RequestError propagation. packages/nax-agent-acp/test/helpers/session-events.ts:5 driveTurn returns an array, and :18 endOf extracts its final turn_end; permission-rejection continuation now asserts that concrete completed event/output against a fake, not a vague promise about a real Gemini process. packages/nax-agent-acp/test/unit/client/backend-permissions.test.ts:181 proves full-profile missing-allow_once denial is existing behavior; for the Gemini continuation case use ask with a caller denial instead of accidentally asserting that full rejects an offered allow_once. The env fallback AC now observes the returned GEMINI_API_KEY and GEMINI_CLI_HOME, leaving real account authentication out of scope. Existing shared env/model-selection code confirms no new consumer call site is needed. Complexity remains complex for each multi-module integration, and security-critical session/access-control/credential handling still mandates three-session-tdd.
outOfScope: Read-only enforcement for pi (the rest of nathapp-io/nax#2372); this spec does not close that issue.
Applying nax's embedder sandbox to gemini, or letting a gemini reviewer run shell commands: under `review` gemini runs in `plan` mode, which offers no shell tool (accepted 2026-10-17).
gemini's `plan` mode writing plan `.md` files into its own plans directory under the gemini home (`.gemini/tmp/…/plans`); those writes never reach the repository and nax does not block them.
gemini's model routing when no model is set: with `auto` it may route `plan`-mode turns to a Pro model, which costs more free-tier quota; nax sets no model unless configured.
Reasoning effort on gemini: it offers no effort config option, so a configured effort is skipped as for any agent that does not offer one.
Copying or translating any other part of the user's gemini home (settings beyond `security.auth.selectedType`, policies, extensions, MCP servers, skills, history) into the isolated home.
Keeping the isolated `settings.json` in step when the user's settings file later loses `selectedType`; a previously written isolated settings file is left in place.
gemini workspace policies (`<repo>/.gemini/policies`): gemini 0.64 disables them by default, and nax neither enables nor checks them.
System or admin gemini settings and policies (`GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH`, the system policies directory); nax does not touch them.
A gemini release that renames `session/set_model`, changes the `models` block shape, or moves auth files; nax does not detect it.
Updating the package context file `.nax/mono/packages/nax-agent-acp/context.md` to say gemini is read-only capable: a manual step after merge, since `.nax/` is read-only to the run.
A live check against a real gemini process: a maintainer step after merge (Google-login and stored-key isolation can only be checked with such an account).
